primary.h1: External check on real ECG no model had seen
primary.label: FROZEN EXTENSION EVIDENCE · REAL UNSEEN ECG · RECORD-LEVEL TARGET · NOT AAMI-SVF · NOT CLINICAL
primary.boundary: Extension outside the locked AAMI_SVF_WINDOW_V1 scope: the dataset has no beat annotations, so the target is record-level (a cardiologist statement or an extra-beat field says the record contains premature beats). No model was trained, selected, calibrated or evaluated on this dataset before; fixed 0.5 rule, no calibration; no clinical, diagnostic or device claim.
models: central V2 + 10 rounds on the original synthetic cohort
central V2 + 10 rounds on the realistic synthetic cohort
primary.table_head: Models on primary (folds 9-10) 4,336 records, 476 with premature beats (prevalence 0.110), 3,809 patients; 95 % patient-cluster bootstrap intervals from 2,000 r
primary.readings: What this showsThe pretrained V2 ranks premature-beat records well above chance on data it never saw (AUROC 0.911, lift 6.4), and clearly better than V1 (V1's paired AUROC change against it is −0.210, interval [-0.237, -0.184], which excludes zero). Adapting a model to a synthetic cohort lowers its performance on this unseen real ECG: original cohort AUROC −0.036, AUPRC −0.169 against the central V2; realistic cohort AUROC −0.046, AUPRC −0.229 against the central V2. A synthetic-cohort candidate is not a better ECG model than the released one. Federated training on real patients matches centralized training in AUROC; see the paired change of the 50-round federated rows.
